# Experiment Design — Surrogate-model scalability & architecture comparison for aerodynamic drag on DrivAerNet++

**Question under test:** Does predictive performance of surrogate models (a) improve with increased training-set size, and (b) differ across architectures, for drag prediction on 26-parameter car designs (fastback / notchback / estateback)?

---

## 1. Rationale
The question decomposes into two hypotheses:
- **H1 (scalability):** for a fixed architecture, test error decreases monotonically as training N grows (learning-curve effect).
- **H2 (architecture):** at a given N, architectures rank differently; and — the interesting case — the ranking *reverses* with N (kernel methods lead at small N, deep nets lead at large N).

Design logic: fix a single held-out test set and a nested stratified training-subset ladder so the *only* thing that changes between points is N (no leakage, no test-set drift). Compare 5 architectures spanning the small-data→large-data spectrum (polynomial floor → GP → tree ensembles → MLP) so a performance crossover, if any, is visible. Report per-body-style to catch whether one style drives the effect.

## 2. Data & Assumptions
**Repository state (verified):** `/workspace` contains only `task.json`. No DrivAerNet++ CSV/HDF5/JSON/README/paper/split/normalisation files are present. All data specifics below are **assumed from the published DrivAerNet++ paper (Saez et al.) and flagged as unverified** — the executing team must confirm against the actual dataset file.

- **Sample size:** assume **~10k total** (range 8k–13k); treat "full" as the actual available N. Per-class counts unknown — assume roughly balanced, verify.
- **26 design parameters:** assume **23 continuous + 3 categorical**. Categoricals: **body style** (fastback/notchback/estateback), **front bumper style**, **rear bumper style**. Continuous: geometric (overhangs, wheelbase, track, height, width, panel angles, wheel diameters/offsets, etc.). *Exact 26 names/split to be confirmed from dataset metadata.*
- **Target:** single scalar **drag coefficient Cd**. (Dataset stores a coefficient vector; we fit/regress only Cd. If multi-output is desired this design must be re-scoped.)
- **Encoding:** one-hot the 3 categoricals (body style → 3 dummies, bumpers → their level counts). Continuous standardized (zero mean / unit var) using **training-subset statistics only** (refit per N to avoid leakage).
- **Body style role:** both an input feature (one-hot) and a stratification axis (balanced draws + per-class metrics). Deliberate choice.
- **No pre-existing splits/normalisation columns assumed** — we create them.

## 3. Models & Hyperparameter policy
Five architectures, ordered by expected data-hunger:

| # | Model | Rationale (scalability tie) |
|---|-------|------------------------------|
| M1 | Linear + deg-2 Polynomial + Ridge (λ via small inner CV) | Cheap floor; shows whether ML beats low-order structure at all. |
| M2 | Gaussian Process, RBF + White kernel, standardized inputs | Small-data champion; O(N³) caps usable N; expected to lead at low N and lose at high N. |
| M3 | Random Forest (n_estimators=400) | Nonparametric, no scaling, parallel; robust mid-N interpolator. |
| M4 | Hist Gradient Boosting (n_estimators=300) | Strongest tree ensemble; better mid/large-N sample efficiency than RF. |
| M5 | MLP 2×128 ReLU, batch-norm, early stopping | Large-data arch; expected to keep improving and overtake GP at high N — the crux of H2. |

**HP policy — two variants:**
- **V1 (HEADLINE): fixed, justified defaults** (values above). No per-model tuning → isolates the pure architecture×size effect; no tuning-budget confound.
- **V2 (sensitivity check): tuned**, each model given an **equal, explicitly-capped inner-CV grid of ≤20 configs total** (5-fold inner CV, selected by inner R²). Explicit grids:
  - M1: Ridge λ ∈ {1e-3, 1e-2, 0.1, 1, 10} (5).
  - M2: length_scale ∈ {0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10}, noise ∈ {1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2} (15).
  - M3: n_estimators ∈ {200, 400}, max_depth ∈ {None, 12}, min_samples_leaf ∈ {1, 2} (8).
  - M4: learning_rate ∈ {0.05, 0.1}, max_iter ∈ {150, 300} (4).
  - M5: hidden ∈ {2×64, 2×128, 2×256}, lr ∈ {1e-3, 3e-4} (6).
  All totals ≤20. **This is a fixed grid, NOT an Optuna/Bayesian sweep.**

## 4. Size ladder & sampling protocol
- **Ladder:** N ∈ **{100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, full}** (7 points; N=5000 added to resolve the mid→high-N transition instead of inferring it).
- **Test set:** one fixed **stratified-by-body-style** held-out set, **20%** of data, shared by all models and all N.
- **Training draws:** remaining 80% = pool. For each N, draw a **nested, stratified, fixed-seed subset** so 100 ⊂ 250 ⊂ … ⊂ 5000 ⊂ full (monotone, no leakage; test never in training).
- **Seeds:** **3 independent draw-seeds** per N to estimate draw-variance; report mean ± std across seeds.
- **Leakage controls:** test disjoint from all training; standardization fit on training subset only; inner-CV folds never touch the test set.

## 5. CV & Evaluation
- **Outer (size-scaling evaluation):** the single fixed held-out test set; metrics computed once per (model, N, seed).
- **Inner (model selection, V2 only):** 5-fold CV on the training subset at each N; folds disjoint from outer test.
- **Metrics:** **RMSE (primary)**, **MAE**, **R²** — reported **both pooled** (all styles) and **per-body-style** (fastback / notchback / estateback).
- **Primary result:** pooled RMSE. Per-class RMSE as secondary to localize architecture differences.

## 6. Analysis plan (mapping to the two sub-questions)
- **Sub-question 1 — scalability trend (H1):**
  - *Figure 1:* learning curves — pooled RMSE vs N (log-x) for each of the 5 architectures, mean ± 3-seed band. Monotone decrease per curve = H1 supported; slope = rate of improvement.
  - *Table 1 (HEADLINE, V1 fixed-defaults):* pooled RMSE/MAE/R² for each model × each N.
- **Sub-question 2 — architecture ranking (H2):**
  - *Figure 2:* same learning curves but with **ranking annotated per N** (rank 1–5 at each N); a visible **crossover** (GP leads at low N, MLP overtakes at high N) is the key evidence.
  - *Table 2:* per-body-style RMSE (model × style × N) to show whether a style drives the ranking.
  - *Table 3 (SENSITIVITY, V2 tuned):* same as Table 1 but with tuned models; compared against Table 1 to show how much the ranking depends on tuning. **Not the primary result.**
- **Statistical note:** with 3 seeds, report whether the low-N (GP) and high-N (MLP) gaps exceed the seed band; if borderline, note as "suggestive, not conclusive" and recommend more seeds.

## 7. Feasibility & Compute budget
- **Env prerequisite (stated plainly):** this design **assumes a pre-provisioned Python env** with `numpy`, `pandas`, `scikit-learn`, and `scikit-optimize` (or equivalent) / `GPyTorch` for the GP. **The current `/workspace` has none of these installed and network is disabled**, so anyone executing this must set up the environment (offline wheels / pre-built venv) **before** running. It is NOT currently available.
- **Fits:** 7 N × 5 models × 3 seeds = **105 outer fits** (V1); V2 multiplies inner-CV selection by the ≤20-config grids per (model, N) but inner fits are cheap.
- **GP wall-clock (heaviest):** at N=2000, O(N³) ≈ 8×10⁹ kernel-eval ops per fit; ×3 seeds ×1 kernel config (V1) ≈ 2.4×10¹⁰ ops. On 224 CPU cores / multithreaded BLAS this is on the order of **seconds-to-a-few-minutes per fit** — comfortably tractable without a GPU. GP is capped at N≤2000 (the 5000 and full points are excluded for the GP, or run with a sparse/inducing-point variant flagged as a variant).
- **MLP:** ≤10k × ~30 encoded features, 2×128, CPU — seconds per fit; trivial.
- **Total:** realistically **< 1–2 wall-clock hours** including V2 tuning; well within budget.

## 8. Limitations
- **Unverified data specifics:** 26-param schema (23+3), per-class counts, total N, and Cd target are assumed from the paper, not inspected (dataset absent from repo). A schema mismatch (e.g., different categorical count) changes encoding and GP kernel design.
- **GP coverage gap:** GP only run to N=2000 due to O(N³); its high-N behavior (5000, full) is not directly measured.
- **Low seed count (3):** draw-variance bands may be too narrow to declare a crossover conclusive; flagged for possible increase.
- **Single held-out test:** one 20% test set gives a point estimate per N; more repeated CV would tighten it at the cost of compute.
- **No environment here:** cannot be executed in the current `/workspace` without first provisioning the Python environment (see §7).
- **Tuning confound:** V1 uses fixed defaults; V2 shows sensitivity but the two use different selection procedures, so V2 is a robustness check, not a fairer headline.
